findings.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/math.ceil on AuditLogEntry.datetime (a datetime). build_cursor calls it on every non-empty page, so every ?optimized_pagination=true request that returns rows fails with an uncaught TypeError (HTTP 500).
findings.evidence: The method copies Paginator.get_item_key, not DateTimePaginator's, which converts to epoch ms. The endpoint uses order_by='-datetime'. paginate() only catches BadPaginationError. Repro: python3 -c "import math,datetime; math.floor(datetime.datetime.now())" raises TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime. Proposed red test: owner, one AuditLogEntry, GET with qs_params={'optimized_pagination':'true'}, expecting 200; it gets 500.
findings.reason: All four seats agree. The repro command ran and fails. Simplest fix: reuse DateTimePaginator or drop the class.

findings.claim: enable_advanced = request.user.is_superuser or organization_context.member.has_global_access runs on every request, before the optimized_pagination flag is checked. organization_context.member can be None, so a non-member caller that passes OrganizationAuditPermission and is not a superuser gets AttributeError (500) on the default endpoint. This regresses existing behaviour.
findings.evidence: RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is documented as None without membership (src/sentry/organizations/services/organization/model.py:344-346). Non-member callers with org:write include legacy org ApiKeys and internal-integration proxy users (src/sentry/sentry_apps/logic.py:351-353). Reasoned. Proposed test: internal-integration token with org:write, GET audit-logs, expecting 200; it gets 500.
findings.reason: Two correctness seats rate it Critical/Important and mattpocock flags the None hazard. It hits the default path with no opt-in needed. Normalised to Critical. Fix: move the check inside the use_optimized branch and guard member is not None.

findings.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor returns the raw integer cursor.value. build_queryset then compares the datetime column with an integer, so cursor-based paging on the optimized path errors or misbehaves. Cursors from DateTimePaginator (epoch ms) are also incompatible.
findings.evidence: DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor (paginator.py:238-241) does the conversion the new class leaves out. Postgres rejects timestamptz <= integer. Reasoned, not executed.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Severity ranges from Critical to Important; normalised to Important because the first page already fails under the get_item_key finding. The same fix (reuse DateTimePaginator) resolves it.

findings.claim: The 'advanced' branch slices the queryset with a user-supplied negative cursor.offset. Django raises ValueError('Negative indexing is not supported.'), which is not converted to a 400, so cursors like 0:-10:0 with optimized_pagination=true return 500. The stated intent ('access to data beyond normal pagination bounds', 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level') is a security hazard, and the comments' claims about Django handling negative slicing are false.
findings.evidence: Cursor.from_string accepts any int offset. Django 5.2.1 is pinned (requirements-frozen.txt:36). QuerySet.__getitem__ rejects negative indexes. Reasoned from Django semantics, not executed. Proposed test: owner GET audit-logs?optimized_pagination=true&cursor=0:-10:0, expecting 400/200; it gets 500.
findings.reason: All four seats agree. No data leak today because Django blocks the slice, but it is a client-triggerable 500 and the intent is unsafe. Remove the negative-offset branch.

findings.claim: The shared BasePaginator.get_result now uses start_offset = max(0, offset) if not cursor.is_prev else offset. This silently clamps negative next-cursor offsets for every Paginator/DateTimePaginator user and still crashes on negative prev offsets. The audit-log feature doesn't need it, and the comment ('queryset will handle boundary conditions') is false.
findings.evidence: Diff hunk at paginator.py:179-184. The duplicate-trim check still uses the raw offset (len(results) == offset + limit + extra) rather than start_offset, so the two diverge. No tests cover it. Reasoned.
findings.reason: Out-of-scope change to shared code with no tests. Revert to the original two lines. If needed, reject negative offsets at the cursor parsing boundary (400).

findings.claim: The admin-only gate is ineffective. has_global_access defaults to True for members, so in practice the gate is just org:write. request.user.is_superuser reads the raw DB flag instead of is_active_superuser(request), bypassing the superuser-session check that the permission class uses.
findings.evidence: src/sentry/models/organizationmember.py:216 (has_global_access default True). src/sentry/api/bases/organization.py:124 uses is_active_superuser(request). Reasoned.
findings.reason: superpowers rated it Important; OCR and mattpocock rated it Minor. Kept at Important because it gates a path whose stated intent is out-of-bounds data access. Use is_active_superuser, or drop the gate along with the feature.

findings.claim: No tests are added for the new paginator class, the new endpoint branch, or the change to the shared BasePaginator.get_result.
findings.evidence: git diff --stat base HEAD -- tests is empty. A grep finds optimized_pagination/OptimizedCursorPaginator only in src. A single smoke test would catch the get_item_key and value_from_cursor failures.
findings.reason: The correctness seat flagged it Important. mattpocock noted that no written repo rule requires tests. Any kept behaviour needs a guarding test.

findings.claim: OptimizedCursorPaginator duplicates BasePaginator.get_result and Paginator's key/cursor methods almost line for line. Its only additions are the broken key handling and the dead negative-offset branch. DateTimePaginator already serves this endpoint, so the class can be deleted (about -95 lines).
findings.evidence: Compare paginator.py:845-911 with paginator.py:135-218 and paginator.py:221-227.
findings.reason: Advisory/over-engineering, non-blocking. Deleting the class is also the smallest fix for the Critical findings.

findings.claim: The patch does not deliver its title ('Enhanced pagination performance'). The new path builds the same queryset, makes the same count call and uses the same slice as the existing path. Nothing in the change improves performance.
findings.evidence: OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result is a near copy of BasePaginator.get_result. The only differences are the broken branches above. Reasoned from the diff.
findings.reason: Advisory spec seat, non-blocking. The resolution is to revert or delete the optimized path rather than keep a misleadingly named feature.

findings.claim: The enable_advanced_features constructor flag has a single caller that always passes True. It is speculative config, and the name doesn't say it enables negative-offset slicing.
findings.evidence: organization_auditlogs.py:82 is the only use. A grep in src/ and tests/ finds no other.
findings.reason: Advisory. Goes away with deleting the class.

findings.claim: The if/else repeats the same self.paginate(...) call. Only paginator_cls and one kwarg differ.
findings.reason: Advisory. Collapses back to the original single call when the optimized path is removed.

findings.claim: A comment-only hunk says negative offsets are now 'allowed'. No behaviour changed (int(offset) already accepted them), so the comment is misleading.
findings.evidence: The cursors.py diff adds 2 comment lines and no code.
findings.reason: Three seats agree. Delete the comment.

findings.claim: Marketing-style or false comments and docstrings: 'sophisticated pagination patterns', 'Django ORM properly handles negative slicing', 'safe because permissions are checked at the queryset level'.
findings.reason: Advisory. The false safety claims are covered by the negative-offset finding. Removed with the class.

findings.claim: Trailing whitespace and a new blank line at EOF break the repo's trailing-whitespace and end-of-file-fixer pre-commit hooks.
findings.evidence: git diff --check 74618671bf HEAD lists organization_auditlogs.py:72 and :89, paginator.py:824, :827, :829, and a new blank line at EOF at paginator.py:912. Hooks are at .pre-commit-config.yaml:175 and :178.
findings.reason: Confirmed by the orchestrator running git diff --check (tooling ground truth, not a gate run).

findings.claim: The new optimized_pagination query parameter is undocumented in API docs or changelog.
findings.evidence: No docs changes in the patch. The endpoint's publish status is EXPERIMENTAL.
findings.reason: ponytail: moot if the optimized path is removed per the findings above. Only document it if the parameter survives.

coverage: Gate not run (benchmark mode: no dependency install and no project checks; only git diff --check was run by the orchestrator to settle the whitespace finding). All four seats reviewed all 3 files in the patch (src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py, src/sentry/api/paginator.py, src/sentry/utils/cursors.py); no files skipped. Untracked sandbox dotfiles in the worktree root (.bashrc, .claude/, .gitconfig, etc.) were excluded from the pinned patch as environment noise. No spec, so the spec axis was judged against the commit title and code comments only. Documented standards are thin (no AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/style guide; only .pre-commit-config.yaml and test-only .cursor rules). Not executed: Django negative-slice behaviour, the integer-vs-timestamptz SQL comparison, the member=None path and all proposed red tests (reasoned only). No other-family (e.g. codex) reviewer was used; all seats are same-family. Rounds 2+, fixes and red tests not run (benchmark mode); no rejection verifier was needed because no correctness Critical/Important finding was rejected.
